    How to Cite ChatGPT in APA, MLA, and Harvard

    Learn how to cite ChatGPT in APA 7, MLA 9, and Harvard referencing with copy-ready examples for in-text citations and reference lists. Complete guide for students.

    cite ChatGPTAPAMLAHarvardAI citationacademic integrity

    As AI tools become part of student workflows, universities now require transparent disclosure of their use. Citing ChatGPT correctly is not just good academic practice — in most institutions it is mandatory. Submitting AI-generated content without attribution is treated as a form of plagiarism and can carry serious academic penalties.

    This guide covers exactly how to cite ChatGPT in APA, MLA, and Harvard formats, with copy-ready examples for in-text citations and reference list entries. Need help ensuring your academic work is fully compliant and properly cited? The experts at Academia Helper can assist.

    Quick Summary: Always cite ChatGPT when using its output in academic work. Use OpenAI as the author, include the model version, the date of your response, and the URL. Formats differ between APA, MLA, and Harvard — examples for each are below.

    Why You Must Cite ChatGPT

    Failing to declare AI use — and presenting its output as your own — is considered a form of academic misconduct by most universities. Beyond policy compliance, citing ChatGPT also:

    • Allows readers to understand how findings or ideas were generated
    • Acknowledges the AI tool's role in your research process
    • Protects you from plagiarism accusations
    • Demonstrates academic transparency and integrity
    ⚠️

    Important: Always check your institution's specific AI use policy first. Some departments and courses prohibit AI-generated content entirely, regardless of citation. Citing does not automatically make AI use acceptable — it depends on your university's current guidelines.

    What You Need to Cite ChatGPT

    Across all citation styles, you will need the same core elements:

    ElementWhat to RecordExample
    Author / CreatorThe company that built the toolOpenAI
    Tool NameThe specific AI tool usedChatGPT
    Model VersionVersion or model usedGPT-4o
    Your PromptThe question or prompt you entered"Explain the impact of inflation on GDP"
    Date of ResponseWhen you received the output15 July 2025
    URLGeneral URL of the toolhttps://chat.openai.com/
    💡

    Best practice: Keep a log of every ChatGPT prompt you use and the responses you receive. Copy or screenshot the full conversation and store it in an appendix if your institution requires it.

    How to Cite ChatGPT in APA 7th Edition

    In APA 7, ChatGPT is treated as a personal communication (non-retrievable) or a software tool (if the output is retrievable via a shared link). For most student use cases — private conversations — treat it as a personal communication.

    In-text citation (personal communication):

    APA In-Text(OpenAI, 2025)

    Reference list entry (retrievable / shared link):

    APA Reference ListOpenAI. (2025). ChatGPT (GPT-4o) [Large language model]. https://chat.openai.com/

    If the conversation is not retrievable, include only the in-text citation with a note such as: [ChatGPT response to the prompt "your question here," 15 July 2025]. Do not add a reference list entry for non-retrievable personal communications.

    How to Cite ChatGPT in MLA (9th Edition)

    MLA treats the prompt you entered as the title of the work and places it in quotation marks.

    Works Cited entry:

    MLA Works Cited"Explain the impact of inflation on GDP." ChatGPT, GPT-4o version, OpenAI, 15 July 2025, chat.openai.com/.

    In-text citation:

    MLA In-Text("Explain the impact")

    MLA shortens the in-text reference to the first few words of the prompt title. Note that MLA also advises disclosing AI tool use in a note or acknowledgement section, particularly for editing or translation use.

    How to Cite ChatGPT in Harvard Referencing

    Harvard style treats ChatGPT as an online software tool.

    Reference list entry:

    Harvard Reference ListOpenAI (2025) ChatGPT (GPT-4o) [online]. Available at: https://chat.openai.com/ (Accessed: 15 July 2025).

    In-text citation:

    Harvard In-Text(OpenAI, 2025)

    Some universities also require you to include your specific prompt in the reference, particularly for assignments where ChatGPT output forms a substantial part of the work.

    Quick Comparison: APA vs MLA vs Harvard

    StyleAuthorIn-TextTitle ElementDate Format
    APA 7OpenAI.(OpenAI, 2025)ChatGPT (GPT-4o)Year only: (2025)
    MLA 9Listed last (OpenAI)("Explain the impact")Your prompt in quotesDay Month Year
    HarvardOpenAI (2025)(OpenAI, 2025)ChatGPT (GPT-4o)Year in author field

    When Do You Need to Cite ChatGPT?

    • You used ChatGPT to generate text that appears in your assignment
    • You used ChatGPT to produce an outline or structure you followed
    • You used ChatGPT to help with paraphrasing or rewording
    • You used ChatGPT for translation or language correction
    • You used ChatGPT to locate or summarise sources (note: always verify those sources independently)

    Final Thoughts

    Citing ChatGPT correctly comes down to three habits: record OpenAI as the author with the model version, follow your required citation style's format, and keep a record of your prompts and responses.
